doc.title: Fred Radke interviewed by Monk Rowe, Hillsdale, Michigan, November 8, 2023

title: Getting the Fiftieth Anniversary tour through Joe Schribman and Joe Graydon
summary: A PBS show with Helen Forrest led to Radke leading the Harry James band, and he reflects on knowing many people.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Managers, bookers and the business of getting work

blocks.x: Well they owned the band business. I think they were the predecessors to Willard Alexander I think, you know from Boston. Joe Schribman was the manager of The Lancers, that’s where I knew him, and he was the last one. And he absolutely loved me. Joe Schribman used to call me up and he’d say, he was serious, he’d go, “Fred.” I said, “Joe” in those days you paid for long distance calls, I said, “Joe why don’t you call first and then call me. Your call would be cheaper.” So there was supposed to be a TV show for PBS in Seattle with Helen Forrest and the Modernnaires and everything. And they were going to use the University of Washington jazz band. And the leader of that band was kind of a jerk. And the music didn’t come in time. So she says, “We’re not going to do it. You’ll have to find somebody else.” So Joe Schribman had booked it with Joe Graydon, who had things with Columbia Artists, and he says, “Well Jeez, get a hold of Fred Radke, I mean I know Fred.” So at the last minute, three days, got my guys and we did this TV show and Helen Forrest was on it and Joe Graydon came up, because he was the producer of the show, and he says, “You know something? I guess — you’re going to hear from me in a couple of days. We’re doing a Fiftieth Anniversary of Harry James and you’re perfect.” And he says, “I know you were with Harry, Joe Schribman thinks a lot of you.” And so a couple of days later he had gone to the estate and they had two different trumpet players that ran the band. And so the last one, I can’t remember who it was, but they said, “Well you’re going out for like four months, the Fiftieth Anniversary national tour. And “No” he said, “we don’t want that kind of — ” And they said, “Well there’s only one person we allow to even think about leading that band,” and he says, “that’s Fred Radke.” He says, “That’s who we want.” So that’s how I got the band. But so when Joe Schribman used to come to Vegas, he came a couple of times, he’d walk in and Harry’d say, “Hey Joe how are you?” He said, “I’m not here to see you, I’m here to see
Fred.” I don’t know, it seems like — not attract but it just seems like obtain a lot of people or something. I don’t know.
You have an extra dose of charm I think.

No I hate to say this but I really know a lot of people. And it’s funny to me. And I really know them. I mean somebody, if you ask me, say hey do you know so-and-so who owns so-and-so do you think you can give me a — yeah sure hey. I have somebody I want you to see right now. Yeah. In fact I’m doing that tomorrow with a couple of students. Somebody’s coming in from Washington, DC and they said, jeez we’re trying to get a position there. I said, “Well do you know” so-and-so. “Oh yeah but.” Well he’s coming to see me Saturday, I’ll put you at his table. What’s it to me? You know.
